name: Missouri
agency: Missouri Department of Revenue (licensing); Missouri State Highway Patrol (driver examinations)
permitAge: 15 (instruction permit; vision, road sign and written tests at an MSHP examination station)

teen.supervisedHours: 40 hours, at least 10 at night between sunset and sunrise (Driver Guide; MoDOT Roadwise)
teen.nightLimit: Intermediate license (16-17): no driving alone 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. (DOR GDL page; some sources: unless with a licensed driver 21+)
teen.passengerLimit: Intermediate: first 6 months no more than 1 passenger under 19 who is not immediate family; after that no more than 3 (DOR 2006 law-change page, marked historical; GHSA)
teen.phone: All drivers: hand-held use banned by the Siddens Bening Hands Free Law (effective Aug 2023, fines from 2025-01-01; secondary enforcement).

notes: Written test: 25 questions, 20 correct to pass (12 CSR 10-24.060). Spanish availability of the test not found; bills to require English-only tests were introduced (HB 2139, HB 1147), outcome not confirmed.
Official Spanish guide: archived 2019 DOR page listed El Manual del Conductor de Missouri (2005); no current official URL found.
Permit supervision under 16: parent, grandparent, guardian or certified instructor; GDL page also lists a qualified driver 25+ licensed 3 years with parental permission.
Intermediate license: all occupants must wear seat belts. Full license at 18.
Rural interstate: SB 1408 (effective 2026-08-28) allows 75 mph on some rural interstates, but MoDOT must study and post; 70 mph remains until signs change.
Move over (RSMo 304.022): change lanes if safe or slow down; covers red/blue and amber vehicles incl. MoDOT.
Headlights required when wipers needed and in fog (RSMo 307.020).
School bus (RSMo 304.050): opposite side of divided highway or four-or-more-lane highway need not stop.
Points: 8 in 18 months = suspension (30/60/90 days); 4 in 12 months = advisory letter (secondary).
Left turn on red from one-way to one-way: status unclear in sources; not used.
